claim: Promoting the 2026 counterterrorism strategy on conservative media, White House counterterrorism director Sebastian Gorka was asked by Breitbart's Alex Marlow whether a right-wing terror threat exists. Gorka answered by naming two Trump critics: "I'm not sure that Nick Fuentes or Tucker Carlson are conservatives... So if you remove those individuals and you understand that they're not conservatives, what's left?" In a separate interview he said of press coverage: "We are moving so fast, they just can't keep up with us, which is delicious." A Newsweek fact-check rated the claim that Gorka named Carlson and Fuentes "possible domestic terrorists" as false — he invoked them when asked about right-wing extremism without applying the label; the White House's response to the story was that "Tucker Carlson is a low-IQ person."

sources.label: Ken Klippenstein — "New Counterterror Strategy Eyes Tucker Carlson" (May 13, 2026).

notes: From @hemurahman_ reel DYU3W7Rxff_. The reel states 'the White House has named Tucker Carlson and Nick Fuentes as potential targets' — that rendering is contested: Klippenstein's headline says the strategy 'eyes' Carlson; Newsweek's fact-check rates the 'possible domestic terrorists' version (as circulated by Alex Jones) false. The record carries Gorka's verbatim words and both characterizations. The 'delicious' quote is from Gorka's interview with Dean Cain, per Klippenstein: 'I did a kind of press call when we released the strategy. 50 articles were written that day about the press call. Only one of them from those putzes at Politico was even slightly negative... We are moving so fast, they just can't keep up with us, which is delicious.' Both Carlson and Fuentes had broken with Trump over the Iran war in the weeks prior.
